channel.title: FZ1073 Incident Monitor (EN)
channel.description: Running overview of public information on the flydubai FZ1073 incident (30 Sep 2026). Distinguishes official, data, media and unconfirmed reports.

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Times of Israel (AAP): Australia probes FZ1073 co-pilot's links to the country
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (Times of Israel, AAP, The Nightly; pages not read directly), Australia's Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team has opened an inquiry into the suspected co-pilot's links to Australia, where media say he studied in 2015–2017. No findings or evidence of a wider network have been published; UAE authorities have not publicly confirmed his identity. (Source: Times of Israel)

item.title: [Media] JPost/Reuters: photo of FZ1073 passengers arriving at Ben Gurion (addendum to u062)
item.description:
[Media] According to the directly read JPost (Reuters) article, the UAE prosecutor general called the incident an attempted terrorist act; this matches u062. Newly recorded medium: a Reuters photo of the plane carrying FZ1073 passengers arriving at Ben Gurion airport on 30 Sep. The article also carries a photo of a damaged rudder credited 'COURTESY'; its origin is unknown. (Source: Jerusalem Post (Reuters))
Photo: Plane carrying passengers from the diverted FZ1073 arrives at Ben Gurion airport, 30 Sep 2026 (REUTERS/AMMAR AWAD, via Jerusalem Post (Reuters))

item.title: [Data] FlightAware: FDB1073 cancelled on 2 Oct, still listed as scheduled for 4 and 5 Oct
item.description: [Data] According to the directly read FlightAware flight history, the Dubai–Tel Aviv service FDB1073 was cancelled on 2 Oct and is listed as scheduled (B39M) for 4 and 5 Oct. These are schedule data only, not confirmation the flights will operate; earlier sources say flydubai suspended Israel flights. (Source: FlightAware)

item.title: [Media] Times of Israel: new cabin video from FZ1073 after the attack was thwarted (Channel 12)
item.description:
[Media] Times of Israel (article read directly) carries new Channel 12 video from the cabin after the attack was thwarted: the wounded captain says he was struck repeatedly, while crew and passengers restrain the attacker. The footage is second-hand and not independently verified; some videos may be graphic. (Source: Times of Israel)
Video: Video from the cabin after the attack was thwarted (Channel 12, via Times of Israel); may be graphic (Channel 12 News / Times of Israel, via Times of Israel)

item.title: [Media] ABC News: FZ1073 second pilot reportedly previously flagged as a security risk
item.description: [Media] ABC News (article read directly), citing unnamed intelligence and law-enforcement officials, reports that the suspected second pilot was taken off flying in 2024 as an Oman Air trainee after extremist materials were found on him, and continued there in an administrative role. The claims come from anonymous sources and are not confirmed by any official body; per search results other outlets repeat them. How he later came to fly for flydubai remains an open question. (Source: ABC News (USA))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Emirates 24|7: flydubai says FZ1073 incident remains under investigation
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to the article (read directly; a media report, not a direct read of the carrier's own site), flydubai says the FZ1073 incident remains under investigation and that the airline is in contact with government agencies and regulators and fully supports the probe. The article brings no new details about the incident. (Source: Emirates 24|7)

item.title: [Media] Reuters/JPost: Israeli investigators expected to take part in questioning the FZ1073 co-pilot in the UAE
item.description: [Media] According to Reuters (read directly on JPost; Ynetnews concurs), the co-pilot was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE on Thursday and Israeli officials are expected to take part in questioning him within the UAE-led investigation, per an unnamed source and an Israeli government official. The text says a motive has not been established; the UAE is examining whether it was a terrorist act or prior planning, and Netanyahu said Israel is checking whether the pilot acted on anyone's direction – these are claims by media and politicians, not verified facts. (Source: Jerusalem Post (Reuters))

item.title: [Media] Gulf News: Saudi Interior Ministry confirms emergency landing at Tabuk and first officer's assault on captain
item.description: [Media] According to the directly read Gulf News article (apparently published 2 Oct), the Saudi Ministry of Interior says it cleared FZ1073 for an emergency landing at Tabuk (174 passengers and 8 crew) and that preliminary investigation found the first officer assaulted the captain, with both injured. Both pilots were taken to Abu Dhabi on 1 Oct after medical clearance. The ministry's statement itself was not read directly; this is the outlet's account. (Source: Gulf News)

item.title: [Media] The National: UAE attorney general says FZ1073 co-pilot attempted a terrorist act
item.description: [Media] According to The National (article read directly), UAE Attorney General Hamad Al Shamsi said the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act, allegedly attacking the captain with a crash axe and trying to take control of the aircraft. The investigation into motive, circumstances and possible links continues. The statement was not read on the prosecution's official site, hence status reported; it is an authority's claim relayed by media. (Source: The National (UAE))

item.title: [Media] Gulf News: GCAA praises FZ1073 captain, crew and passengers; Public Prosecution leads the investigation
item.description: [Media] According to Gulf News (article read directly), the GCAA praised the courage and quick response of the captain, crew and passengers who helped bring the situation under control. The captain has returned to the UAE, is in good condition and receiving care. A Public Prosecution team leads the investigation; the GCAA declines to comment on details or claims and urges reliance on official sources only. The statement was not read on the GCAA site, hence status reported. (Source: Gulf News)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Emirates 24|7: flydubai CEO confirms official FZ1073 investigation
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to the article (read directly), the flydubai CEO said a security incident occurred in the cockpit of FZ1073 and that a comprehensive official investigation is underway; he praised the captain and crew. The airline is reported to have suspended Tel Aviv operations until the investigation concludes. This is a news site's retelling, not a statement read directly on flydubai's own site, hence unconfirmed. (Source: Emirates 24|7)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Mako: Oman reportedly previously barred FZ1073 first officer from flying
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to a headline in search results (page not read directly), Israeli site Mako reports that Oman had earlier barred the first officer from flying. This is a single source with no confirmation from UAE, KSA or Omani authorities, and the details and the claim's origin are unknown. (Source: Mako (N12))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Israel Hayom: FZ1073 co-pilot reportedly confessed under questioning to planning to crash the aircraft
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly), Israel Hayom cites an unconfirmed report that the Omani co-pilot admitted during questioning in Saudi Arabia to intending to crash the aircraft in Israel. Hebrew search results (Mako) similarly mention preliminary findings of a nationalist motive and radicalisation; UAE and Saudi authorities have not confirmed this and it rests on a single source. (Source: Israel Hayom)

item.title: [Media] Al Jazeera: reconstruction of FZ1073's 12 minutes – captain and passengers intervene
item.description: [Media] According to the article (read directly), the crisis unfolded roughly between 05:21 and 05:33 GMT and the landing at Tabuk took place around 06:58 GMT. The media report a drop of about 17,000 ft in two minutes (conflicting with FR24: >14,000 ft in <30 s) and that the wounded captain opened the cockpit door, after which passengers subdued the attacker and one briefly controlled the aircraft. Based on passenger accounts and politicians' statements, not independently verified. (Source: Al Jazeera)

item.title: [Media] Fortune: FZ1073 raises questions about crew vetting and cockpit security
item.description: [Media] According to the article (read directly), Netanyahu acknowledged a "loophole" and Israel will now vet all pilots flying into the country. Fortune also says the crew reported a hijacking to air traffic control and requested ambulances, and that initial landing requests in Saudi Arabia and Jordan were refused before Tabuk was approved. It gives 182 people on board, another discrepancy with earlier figures (174 / ~150 / ~180). This is the media's account. (Source: Fortune)

item.title: [Media] CBS: Omani official confirms first officer's origin; investigators probe whether he acted alone
item.description: [Media] According to the article (read directly), an unnamed Omani official told CBS the first officer was born in Oman and holds Omani citizenship; the Omani government has not publicly confirmed this. CBS says the suspect was transferred to the UAE for questioning and investigators are examining whether he acted alone. Netanyahu said he believes the man was radicalized and did not rule out that he was "dispatched"; he called an Iran link premature. These are officials' claims relayed by the media; no motive has been officially published. (Source: CBS News)

item.title: [Media] The National: FZ1073 puts pilot "deadheading" in the spotlight
item.description: [Media] According to the article (read directly), two off-duty pilots travelling as passengers on FZ1073 helped with the landing at Tabuk. The piece examines the practice of positioning crews as passengers, which analyst Saj Ahmad says has become more common in the Gulf; it cites a descent of about 17,400 ft. This is the outlet's analysis, not an official finding. (Source: The National (UAE))

item.title: [Media] AP: attack on FZ1073 pilot raises questions over crew vetting and cockpit doors
item.description:
[Media] The AP (article read directly) quotes security experts: pilot vetting varies worldwide and may not match passenger screening; reinforced post-9/11 cockpit doors make outside intervention hard when the threat is inside. According to the article, the Omani first officer reportedly bypassed Israeli safeguards against pilots from countries without diplomatic ties; this is a claim in the article, not a confirmed fact. It adds no new facts on the cause. (Source: AP přes ABC News (USA))
Photo: Israeli passenger arriving at Ben Gurion airport after the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, 30 Sept 2026. (AP Photo/Ariel Schalit, via AP přes ABC News (USA))

item.title: [Media] JPost: some Israelis refused to board the rescue flight, Saudis did not permit the Israeli air force
item.description:
[Media] According to JPost (read directly), some Israeli passengers initially refused to board flydubai's replacement flight from Tabuk because it was not operated by an Israeli aircraft; of 174 passengers, 166 were reportedly Israelis (per Israeli media). The article says Saudi authorities refused to let the Israeli air force fly in, and a 51-year-old passenger was taken to hospital with a mild injury on arrival; the details come from unnamed sources and media and are not officially confirmed. (Source: Jerusalem Post)
Photo: Arrival of the rescue flight with FZ1073 passengers at Ben Gurion Airport, 30 Sep 2026 (Section 27A (podle popisku JPost), via Jerusalem Post)

item.title: [Media] JPost: Omani first officer of FZ1073 held no second nationality
item.description: [Media] According to JPost (read directly), unnamed sources familiar with the investigation say the suspected Omani F/O held no other nationality and that the Israel-UAE aviation agreement, in their account, does not require pilots from countries with ties to Israel. This contradicts an earlier claim by a source at Israel's transport ministry; neither UAE nor Omani authorities have confirmed it. (Source: Jerusalem Post)

item.title: [Media] JPost: why four pilots were aboard FZ1073
item.description: [Media] According to JPost (read directly), two additional pilots were aboard because of possible route extensions and crew duty-time limits, not because of a security warning; the source is an unnamed person. A passenger quoted by the paper says one of the extra pilots took control; the sequence inside the cockpit has not been independently confirmed. This addresses the open question about the additional pilot. (Source: Jerusalem Post)

item.title: [Media] Lead Stories: viral video of FZ1073 passengers "celebrating" is from August 2025, not the incident
item.description: [Media] According to a directly read Lead Stories fact-check (1 Oct 2026), a video circulated on social media as showing FZ1073 passengers celebrating after the hijacking attempt actually shows the Israeli men's basketball team on a plane in 2025 (originally Sport5). This is a disinformation warning; it adds nothing new about the incident itself. (Source: Lead Stories (fact-check))

item.title: [Media] JPost: Israeli agencies reportedly believe in a "lone wolf", not Iranian direction
item.description: [Media] The Jerusalem Post (article read directly, updated Oct 1) says several unnamed sources from the Mossad, Shin Bet, the military and the transport ministry believe the attacker was a lone actor not acting on orders from Iran or a terror group. These are claims by anonymous Israeli sources, not an official conclusion; they conflict with suspicions of other involvement (u044) and hints at Iran (u046), and neither the UAE nor Saudi investigations have confirmed them. (Source: Jerusalem Post)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Arabian Business: Saudi preliminary investigation says F/O assaulted the captain
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly, server returned error 405), Arabian Business reports that Saudi authorities' preliminary investigation concluded the co-pilot assaulted the captain and both were injured. Per the article the Saudi statement gives no motive; this is a single-outlet claim and the Saudi statement itself was not read directly. (Source: Arabian Business (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] CNN: Trump suggests possible Iran link for FZ1073 second pilot, no evidence given
item.description: [Media] According to CNN's live coverage (read directly), US President Trump, asked whether the pilot may be linked to Iran, said that "based on what he is hearing" yes, but that they are still working on it; he gave no details. Israeli PM Netanyahu called it too early to assess any Iranian role, the UAE is investigating a possible link to terrorism, and the motive remains unknown. These are political claims, not a verified finding; follows u038. (Source: CNN)

item.title: [Media] ABC: FZ1073 descent reconstruction cites over 20,000 ft, repeated drops
item.description: [Media] ABC News (article read directly) describes repeated drops that a passenger likened to a nosedive, citing a height loss of over 20,000 ft and a final descent to about 5,000 ft; it relies on Israeli officials, passengers and flydubai. This differs from FR24 (>14,000 ft in <30 s) and from other sources (17,000 ft in ~2 min); the discrepancy remains unresolved. ABC says 174 people were on board. (Source: ABC News (Australia))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Israel Hayom: new suspicion that the FZ1073 first officer did not act alone
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to the headline of an Israel Hayom article in search results, a new suspicion has emerged in the investigation that this was not a lone act. The page was not read directly (403), so its content and sources are unknown; the Israeli site Mako similarly says certainty is lacking but suspicion of a nationalist motive is growing. These are unverified media speculation, not confirmed by the UAE or KSA. (Source: Israel Hayom (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] CNN: suspect co-pilot and injured captain both flew from Saudi Arabia to Abu Dhabi
item.description: [Media] CNN (live blog read directly), citing the Saudi Interior Ministry, reports that both pilots, once medically cleared, left Tabuk for Abu Dhabi on Thursday accompanied by a UAE security team. According to the ministry, the preliminary Saudi investigation with UAE team participation found an assault on the captain by the co-pilot; the motive and weapon have not been disclosed and authorities have not named the suspect. (Source: CNN)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Al Arabiya: passengers left Tabuk on a replacement aircraft and reached Israel
item.description:
[Unconfirmed] Al Arabiya posted a video on YouTube saying FZ1073 passengers left Tabuk on a replacement aircraft and arrived in Israel. The video was not played; the title comes from the preview (oEmbed). (Source: Al Arabiya)
Video: passengers departing Tabuk on a replacement aircraft (Al Arabiya (YouTube), via Al Arabiya)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] 9 News Australia video: pilot stabbed by another pilot on the Dubai–Tel Aviv flight
item.description:
[Unconfirmed] Australian broadcaster 9 News posted a report on YouTube about the alleged stabbing of a pilot on FZ1073. The video was not played or verified; the title comes from the preview (oEmbed). Some videos may be graphic. (Source: 9 News Australia (YouTube))
Video: report on the alleged stabbing of a pilot (9 News Australia (YouTube), via 9 News Australia (YouTube))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] CBS News video: cabin footage and the fight for control of the aircraft
item.description:
[Unconfirmed] CBS News on YouTube shares footage shot by passengers in the cabin of FZ1073 after the alleged stabbing of a pilot. I read the video title only from the preview (oEmbed); the video itself was not played or verified, and the author of the original footage is unknown. Some videos may be graphic. (Source: CBS News (YouTube))
Video: cabin footage (title: passengers' fight for control of the aircraft) (CBS News (YouTube); původní autor záběrů není znám, via CBS News (YouTube))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Cabin video: screaming and confusion on approach to landing
item.description:
[Unconfirmed] The aggregator Cedar News carries a cabin video in which passengers can be heard screaming amid commotion as the aircraft approaches land. The author is not named and the content has not been verified; the page was read via WebFetch. (Source: Cedar News)
Video: cabin footage during approach to landing (autor ve zdroji neuveden, via Cedar News)

item.title: [Media] Haaretz: Netanyahu claims FZ1073 co-pilot underwent "Islamist radical indoctrination"
item.description: [Media] According to the directly read Haaretz article, the Israeli prime minister said in a Fox News interview that the co-pilot underwent radical Islamist indoctrination; ABC, CBS and Al-Monitor carry the same claim consistently (per search results). This is a claim by an Israeli official that the UAE and Saudi Arabia have not confirmed; per ABC, Netanyahu added he is not drawing final conclusions, and Israeli officials have not confirmed Iranian involvement and preliminarily assume a lone actor. (Source: Haaretz)

item.title: [Media] Khaleej Times: GCAA urges against sharing unofficial information, will publish findings
item.description: [Media] According to the Khaleej Times article (read directly), the GCAA says its review of operational and security aspects of FZ1073 continues and it will publish results once complete. It asks the public not to circulate unofficial information or pre-empt conclusions. The statement was not read directly on the GCAA site, so this is a media report; no investigation lead has been announced yet. (Source: Khaleej Times)

item.title: [Media] The National: FZ1073 incident reopens debate on cockpit video recorders
item.description: [Media] According to the article (read directly), the incident revived debate on mandatory cockpit video recorders; aircraft currently need only audio and data recorders and no international video mandate exists. An FAA panel recommended against a mandate in August 2025 citing pilot-union concerns. This is a general policy debate, not a finding about the incident. (Source: The National (UAE))

item.title: [Media] Al Jazeera: how the FZ1073 co-pilot was cleared to fly
item.description: [Media] The article (read directly) explains that the co-pilot met GCAA UAE requirements for licence, Class 1 medical and language proficiency; experts note such checks are a snapshot in time and may not detect behavioural problems. It says the UAE ordered an investigation into motives and that Israeli officials initially suggested terrorism but evidence is not yet sufficient. This is analysis and expert opinion, not an investigation result. (Source: Al Jazeera)

item.title: [Media] Saudi Gazette: Saudi NTSC opens safety investigation into Tabuk landing (clarifies u025)
item.description: [Media] According to the directly read Saudi Gazette article, the Saudi National Transport Safety Center said it received a report of the incident and sent an investigation team to establish circumstances and evidence from an aviation-safety perspective. The article also says the UAE runs a separate criminal investigation led by the Attorney General, to examine motives and any link to terrorism. This is a retelling of agency reporting; the center's own statement was not read directly. (Source: Saudi Gazette)

item.title: [Official] UAE MoFA: monitoring FZ1073 incident, Attorney General ordered investigation
item.description: [Official] The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (text read directly via WebFetch) says it is monitoring the incident and that the Attorney General ordered an investigation team. It states UAE law applies to the UAE-registered aircraft even outside UAE territory, and the probe is to cover possible terrorism links, planning or external direction. It urges the public to rely only on official sources. (Source: Ministerstvo zahraničních věcí SAE (MoFA))

item.title: [Media] Arab News: UAE probe to assess terrorism; captain opened cockpit door
item.description: [Media] Arab News (article read directly) says the attacker was an Omani national and the injured captain opened the cockpit door, allowing passengers to restrain the attacker; 174 people were aboard. The UAE probe is to determine whether it was terrorism or planned, Netanyahu reportedly said it is too early to say who is behind it, and India's prime minister called the pilot a hero. These are media-relayed claims; nationality and sequence are not verified by authorities. (Source: Arab News)

item.title: [Media] CNN: suspect expected to be handed to UAE, axe weapon unconfirmed, Ben Gvir demands extradition to Israel
item.description: [Media] CNN (live blog read directly) quotes Israeli PM Netanyahu: the suspect was detained by Saudi authorities and Netanyahu expects him to be transferred to the UAE for questioning with Israeli involvement; he called the use of an axe unconfirmed. An Israeli official told CNN the first officer had worked at flydubai for eight months. Minister Ben Gvir demands the suspect be extradited to Israel; the UAE bases jurisdiction on the aircraft's registration. These are claims by Israeli officials relayed by the media, not verified investigation findings. (Source: CNN)

item.title: [Media] UAE Attorney-General orders investigation team for FZ1073
item.description: [Media] According to a Dubai Eye article (read directly), the UAE Attorney-General ordered a Public Prosecution team to establish the motives of the incident and assess possible premeditation or terrorist links, in coordination with the GCAA. The UAE bases jurisdiction on the aircraft being UAE-registered. The Attorney-General urged the public not to spread speculation. The statement text itself was not read on an official site. (Source: Dubai Eye 103.8)

item.title: [Media] CNN: Israel calls it a terror attack, motive unconfirmed; El Al preparing evacuation flights from Dubai
item.description: [Media] CNN (live blog read directly) says Israel calls the incident an attempted terrorist attack, but no motive is confirmed and the attacker has not been officially identified; one Israeli official says he is an Omani national. CNN reports the plane fell 17,400 ft in under two minutes (conflicts with FR24's >14,000 ft in <30 s). El Al is preparing to evacuate Israelis from Dubai, no date set; flydubai operated about 70 flights a week on the route. (Source: CNN)

item.title: [Media] Newsweek: Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia says captain's condition is stable
item.description: [Media] According to Newsweek (article read directly), citing AP, the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said the captain is in stable condition; Israeli media reportedly write of surgery for his wounds. This is relayed information not verified by the maintainer; no official medical report was found. (Source: Newsweek (přes AP))

item.title: [Media] Emirates suspends codeshare flights with flydubai to Tel Aviv
item.description: [Media] According to Gulf News (article read directly), Emirates has suspended its codeshare operations with flydubai to and from Tel Aviv with immediate effect until further notice. Passengers whose final destination is Tel Aviv will not be accepted at their origin; those already en route will be supported to complete their journeys. Khaleej Times reports the same (search results only). (Source: Gulf News)

item.title: [Media] ABC: Netanyahu praises injured captain, cause still unknown per flydubai
item.description: [Media] According to ABC (article read directly), the Israeli prime minister claims the injured captain opened the cockpit door, which let passengers and crew overpower the attacker. ABC says flydubai states the underlying reasons remain unknown and warns against premature conclusions. ABC also reports that Saudi Arabia arrested one pilot and that it is unexplained how a weapon got on board; these are claims by Israeli officials and media, not official investigation findings, and no lead investigating authority has published any yet. (Source: ABC News (Australia))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Saudi national transport safety centre opens investigation into Tabuk landing
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (page not read directly, site returns 403), Saudi outlet Sabq reports that the national transport safety centre has opened an investigation into the FZ1073 emergency landing at Tabuk and an investigation team has begun work with the relevant authorities. No directly read statement from the centre confirms this yet; the relationship to the GCAA UAE investigation is not specified. (Source: Sabq (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] Al Jazeera: FZ1073 timeline, attack claim not independently confirmed
item.description: [Media] According to Al Jazeera (read directly), unusual manoeuvres began at 05:21Z, squawk 7700 at 05:28Z and 7500 at 05:35Z, landing in Tabuk at 06:45Z. The outlet describes Netanyahu's claim of a pilot stabbing and attempt to crash the aircraft as not independently confirmed, as is the Omani nationality of the other pilot. Squawk times differ slightly from other sources (05:31Z / 05:38Z), and the opposition (Lapid) questions political use of the incident. (Source: Al Jazeera)

item.title: [Official] flydubai (official site): cockpit altercation and suspension of Israel flights
item.description: [Official] The flydubai official website (read directly) carries three statements: the aircraft landed safely in Tabuk, an altercation occurred in the flight deck and was contained by the crew, and all passengers and crew are safe. The carrier is suspending flights to and from Israel in coordination with authorities while the investigation continues. This confirms earlier reports (u010, u022); it gives no cause or identities. (Source: flydubai News)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] flydubai temporarily suspends all flights to and from Israel
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to a Dubai Eye article (read directly; the flydubai statement on its own website has not yet been read directly), the carrier temporarily suspended all flights to and from Israel in coordination with the relevant authorities so the FZ1073 investigation can continue. It apologised to affected passengers and said it would review the suspension as more information emerges. (Source: Dubai Eye 103.8)

item.title: [Media] GCAA UAE: 'security incident' on FZ1073 brought under control, crew members injured
item.description: [Media] According to Gulf News (read directly), the UAE GCAA said flight FZ1073 experienced a security incident that was brought under control, and the aircraft made an emergency landing at Tabuk. Some crew members were injured and treated at a Saudi hospital; GCAA investigation teams are working with relevant authorities on causes and circumstances. The statement text on the GCAA website itself was not read directly (the page contained nothing on it), so this is a media report, not status official; it is the first GCAA statement found on the incident. (Source: Gulf News (cituje prohlášení GCAA UAE))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] New onboard videos and photos from Tabuk
item.description:
[Unconfirmed] Media have published more footage: a passenger's video shortly before landing, a video of passengers intervening and a cabin video during the descent (shared on X), a photo of passengers disembarking in Tabuk and, per search results, photos of the damaged rudder (Times of Israel; page not read directly). The directly read One Mile at a Time also mentions rudder damage; it is not officially confirmed (see u006). No one has officially verified the origin or authenticity of the footage; some videos may be graphic. (Source: Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Video: Passenger films the situation after the attacker was subdued, shortly before landing in Tabuk (unverified) (autor ve zdroji neuveden (via Israel National News), via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Video: Onboard video: passengers intervene (The Daily Telegraph, YouTube Shorts; unverified) (The Daily Telegraph (AU), via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Video: Cabin video during the steep descent, screaming audible (shared on X, original author unknown; unverified) (Heidi Bachram (@HeidiBachram) na X, původní autor neuveden, via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Photo: Passengers disembark in Tabuk (lead photo of The Media Line article; unverified) (sociální sítě (dle popisku The Media Line), via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)
Photo: Photos of the tail after landing – damaged rudder (Times of Israel, per search results; unverified) (autor ve zdroji neuveden, via Israel National News / The Media Line / One Mile at a Time / The Daily Telegraph / Times of Israel)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Media: two off-duty pilots travelling as passengers reportedly broke into the cockpit
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (pages not read directly), media reportedly say two off-duty pilots travelling as passengers (one South African, one from New Zealand) got into the cockpit with help from cabin crew and passengers and restrained the other pilot. These are individual websites, not confirmed by authorities or flydubai; one search also cites a descent from FL340 to about 19,000 ft in ~90 s, yet another variant among the conflicting descent profiles. (Source: Newsweek / Migflug / Cedar News (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] Tabuk Airport: all passengers departed on a replacement aircraft, both pilots in hospital
item.description: [Media] According to Saudi Gazette (article read directly), Tabuk airport says the distress call came at 08:44 local time, the aircraft landed at 09:45 and all passengers left on a replacement aircraft at 17:40. Both the captain and the co-pilot were injured and taken to hospital; the airport says the competent authorities are investigating. The article also repeats flydubai's statement that causes and motives are unknown. (Source: Saudi Gazette)

item.title: [Media] Israeli Defense Minister Katz: attempted terrorist attack; flydubai urges no speculation
item.description: [Media] According to Ynetnews (article read directly), Defense Minister Katz called the incident an attempted "jihadist terrorist attack" and said the intent was to crash the aircraft; this is a claim by an Israeli official, not a confirmed fact. Flydubai, by contrast, says the causes and motives are unknown and subject to an official investigation, and urges against speculation. Israeli passengers left Tabuk on a replacement flight after Mossad vetted the crew. (Source: Ynetnews)

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Second flydubai flight to Tel Aviv: media say tracking glitch
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (pages not read directly), hours after FZ1073 reports emerged that another flydubai flight was turning back from Tel Aviv. Media say it was a glitch on flight-tracking sites and flight FZ1081 continued normally; there is no official confirmation. (Source: The Week / Business Today / Cedar News (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Media] Netanyahu: pilot stabbed the other and was arrested by the Saudis
item.description: [Media] According to search results (JPost, AFP and others; pages not read directly), Israeli PM Netanyahu said one pilot stabbed the other, apparently tried to crash the plane or sabotage its systems, and was arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities. This is a claim by the Israeli side; UAE/KSA and investigators have not officially confirmed it, and it conflicts with the AvHerald headline (u014) about a suspected suicide attempt. (Source: Jerusalem Post / AFP / další (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] AvHerald updates headline: F/O under investigation for suspected suicide attempt
item.description: [Unconfirmed] At 09:59Z AvHerald changed its article headline to “first officer under investigation for suspected suicide attempt” (previously only “fight in the cockpit”). Only the headline on AvHerald's official Bluesky account was read directly, not the article itself – who is leading the investigation and what the headline is based on is unknown. This contradicts the Israeli assessment of a possible terrorist act; none of it is officially confirmed. Supplements u009. (Source: The Aviation Herald (titulek na Bluesky @avherald.com))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Israel: joint investigation, origin of pilots' passports also examined
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (pages not read directly), Mossad, Shin Bet, the military and the transport ministry are involved in the investigation in Israel, which assesses the incident as a possible terror attack. Israeli media say the first officer had worked at flydubai for about nine months, and the transport minister has asked for a check of compliance with agreements on pilots holding passports of states with diplomatic ties to Israel; none of this is officially confirmed. (Source: Israel Hayom / Kan / Reuters (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Conflict: captain's nationality – Indian vs. Emirati
item.description: [Unconfirmed] Indian media, according to search results (pages not read directly) and citing Israeli sources, say the captain is Indian. This contradicts entry u011, where an Israeli official (via CNN) described the captain as a UAE citizen. Neither claim has been officially confirmed. (Source: The Week / India TV (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Israeli official: captain from the UAE, second pilot from Oman; media describe stab wound
item.description: [Unconfirmed] Media citing an Israeli official say the captain is a UAE national and the second pilot an Omani national, and that it is suspected the second pilot tried to crash the aircraft. Some reports mention a stab wound to the captain and two off-duty pilots among the passengers who helped; none of this is officially confirmed and details differ from earlier reports. Content was not read directly. (Source: CNN / Reuters (přes vyhledávání))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] flydubai: emergency caused by altercation between pilots, investigation opened
item.description: [Unconfirmed] According to search results (the carrier's page was not read directly) flydubai says the emergency signal was triggered by a violent altercation between the pilots, the aircraft landed safely in Tabuk and passengers are fine. The carrier reportedly opened its own investigation and sent a replacement aircraft to Tabuk. (Source: flydubai (news.flydubai.com))

item.title: [Unconfirmed] AvHerald and ASN have an entry – content not available for automated reading
item.description: [Unconfirmed] Both sites block automated access, so the monitor only picks up changes to these entries indirectly (via search). (Source: The Aviation Herald / ASN)

item.title: [Media] Euronews: Israeli officials speak of an averted disaster
item.description: [Media] Summary of witness accounts of one pilot being stabbed and the Israeli suspicion of a terrorist act. (Source: Euronews)

item.title: [Media] Video: injured passenger's account
item.description:
[Media] Video of a passenger describing the attack in the cockpit. The video content has not been verified; the source is an aggregator. (Source: Cedar News)
Video: passenger's account (via Cedar News)

item.title: [Media] Tabuk airport: both pilots injured; Israel asks to halt flydubai flights
item.description:
[Media] JPost cites a Tabuk airport statement that both pilots were injured and taken to hospital. Transport Minister M. Regev asked Shin Bet to suspend flydubai flights. It also mentions a photo of a damaged rudder – not technically verified, unconfirmed. (Source: Jerusalem Post)
Photo: damaged rudder per JPost (unconfirmed) (autor ve zdroji neuveden, via Jerusalem Post)

item.title: [Media] Passenger describes subduing the attacker in the cockpit
item.description: [Media] A passenger (CEO of Barak Capital Underwriting) says he entered the cockpit with other men and a relief pilot and overpowered the attacker. This is a witness account, not an investigation finding. (Source: Ctech (Calcalist))

item.title: [Media] Israel: suspicion the F/O tried to crash the aircraft
item.description:
[Media] According to the Israeli assessment the F/O (reportedly from Oman) is the suspect. Contact with Saudi Arabia is handled by Mossad. Ynet says flydubai described the incident as a scuffle between pilots and opened its own investigation – that statement is not yet visible in other sources. (Source: Ynetnews)
Photo: illustrative flydubai photo (2024), not from the incident (Photofex_AUT / Shutterstock.com, via Ynetnews)

item.title: [Media] Israeli sources: not a hijacking
item.description: [Media] Early Israeli reports ruled out a hijacking; the explanation was said to be a cockpit altercation. No statement in the flydubai newsroom at that time. Ynet: 174 PAX incl. 27 children; the aircraft briefly entered Jordanian airspace and turned back. (Source: AeroCorner)

item.title: [Data] FR24: flight ADS-B data, squawk 7700 → 7500 → 7700
item.description:
[Data] Departure 03:05Z, FL340, last ADS-B 06:58Z after landing in Tabuk. The blog offers a CSV with barometric altitude, GS and vertical speed – useful for your own analysis of the descent profile. (Source: Flightradar24 blog)
Photo: FR24 extended timeline (X) (Flightradar24 (@flightradar24), via Flightradar24 blog)
Video: FR24 flight playback (Flightradar24, via Flightradar24 blog)

item.title: [Official] flydubai confirms incident and safe landing in Tabuk
item.description:
[Official] A flydubai spokesperson confirmed an incident on FZ1073 DXB–TLV, a safe landing at TUU and that all passengers are fine. No cause given. The article cites KAN on a 'fight between pilots' – per AeroTime not independently confirmed. (Source: AeroTime)
Photo: illustrative flydubai B38M (not A6-FKF) (Markus Mainka / Shutterstock.com, via AeroTime)
Photo: FR24 timeline (X) (Flightradar24 (@flightradar24), via AeroTime)
